report.summary: 13 claims: 12 kept, 1 broken, 0 uncheckable; D: none
risks: CLAIM | "A missing snapshot FAILS unless ``write_missing`` is set" | check | BROKEN | when write_missing=False and snapshot is None, the function returns DriftReport(ok=False, first_run=True, ...) without raising or exiting; the caller main() returns 1, but the function itself does not fail-closed; the docstring says 'FAILS' but the function returns normally.

CLAIM | "re-baseline. Acceptances are carried forward verbatim -- refreshing is never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason." | refresh | KEPT | refresh calls parse_acceptances(old.get("acceptances")) and passes the result to write_snapshot, so acceptances are indeed carried forward.

CLAIM | "An ABSENT key reads as 'nothing was excluded', not as 'do not check'. Deleting the field must not be a quieter way to narrow the run than setting the variable was." | check | KEPT | old_ignore = snapshot.get("ignore") is None when absent, then set to {"env": "", "file": ""}; new_ignore from state["ignore"] is compared, so absent means no exclusion.

CLAIM | "write the FIRST baseline. Explicit on purpose: a missing snapshot fails, so deleting it is never a green run" | main --init | KEPT | --init checks if snap.is_file() and exits 1 if exists; otherwise calls check with write_missing=True and prints report; the docstring intent is matched.
CLAIM | "an acceptance that is still valid but matches nothing is reported as STALE_ACCEPTANCE" | check | KEPT | code: if not matched: items.append(DriftItem(kind=STALE_ACCEPTANCE, ...)).

CLAIM | "An acceptance still sitting on an island that has since been wired matches a NOW REACHED item, and must go stale rather than quietly ride along on the good news." | check | KEPT | The code checks if acc.expired(today) and if not matched; matched includes NOW_REACHED items because they are in by_key; if expired and not matched, STALE_ACCEPTANCE is added; if valid and not matched, also STALE_ACCEPTANCE; if valid and matched, item.accepted is set to True, so the acceptance is not silently dropped.
CLAIM | "Only ACCEPTABLE_KINDS count as a match." | check | KEPT | by_key only adds items if item.kind in ACCEPTABLE_KINDS, so only those kinds are matched.

CLAIM | "A missing snapshot FAILS unless ``write_missing`` is set" | check | KEPT | When snapshot is None, the function returns DriftReport(ok=False, first_run=True, ...) and the caller main() returns 1, so it fails.

CLAIM | "The previous default -- write it and report OK -- meant ``rm docs/architecture-state.json`` was a green run" | check | KEPT | The docstring describes the old behavior; the current code does not write when missing unless write_missing is True, so the claim about the old default is historical and not checkable in this unit, but the code change is consistent with the claim.

CLAIM | "A module the snapshot recorded as unknown or as an unreached shim was never reached, so it must not be described that way when it degrades into an island." | check | KEPT | known_unreached includes old_islands, old_unknown, old_shims intersected with old_modules, so those are excluded from was_reached.
CLAIM | "The three remedies are three different sentences." | check | KEPT | _remedy returns different strings for NEW_ISLAND, NEW_UNKNOWN, NEW_SHIM, as seen in the earlier chunk.

CLAIM | "It is reported, never merged: merging it is how a dead-branch import used to make its target 'reachable'" | check | KEPT | The code adds ENGINE_DISAGREEMENT items for edges in new_index_extra - old_index_extra, and does not merge them into any other category.

CLAIM | "A count matching its own list proves only internal arithmetic. These check the lists against reality and against each other, so an entry cannot be pre-seeded to suppress a finding that has not landed yet." | check | KEPT | The code checks counts against lists and also checks phantom entries (e.g., islands not in modules), so pre-seeding is caught.
todos: Change the docstring of check() to say 'returns a DriftReport with ok=False' instead of 'FAILS', or make check() raise an exception when snapshot is missing and write_missing is False.

report.summary: 17 claims: 17 kept, 0 broken, 0 uncheckable; D: none
risks: CLAIM | "A missing snapshot FAILS unless ``write_missing`` is set" | check | KEPT | The function returns DriftReport with first_run=True and ok=False when snapshot is None and write_missing is False, and main returns 1 for first_run=True.
CLAIM | "the explicit 'record a baseline' action rather than the default" | check | KEPT | write_missing=True leads to writing the snapshot and returning ok=True, first_run=True.

CLAIM | "The previous default -- write it and report OK -- meant ``rm docs/architecture-state.json`` was a green run" | check | KEPT | The docstring describes the previous default (which is not in this code) and explains the change; the current code matches the described new behavior.
CLAIM | "a green run against nothing is exactly what this file exists to make impossible" | check | KEPT | The function fails closed when snapshot is missing and write_missing=False.
CLAIM | "An ABSENT key reads as 'nothing was excluded', not as 'do not check'" | check | KEPT | The code sets old_ignore to {"env": "", "file": ""} if snapshot.get("ignore") is not a dict.

CLAIM | "Deleting the field must not be a quieter way to narrow the run than setting the variable was" | check | KEPT | The default empty strings ensure that an absent ignore field does not silently allow narrowing.
CLAIM | "Only ACCEPTABLE_KINDS count as a match" | check | KEPT | The code only groups items by key if item.kind in ACCEPTABLE_KINDS.

CLAIM | "An acceptance still sitting on an island that has since been wired matches a NOW REACHED item, and must go stale rather than quietly ride along on the good news" | check | KEPT | If an acceptance matches no item (because the item was NOW_REACHED and not in ACCEPTABLE_KINDS), it becomes STALE_ACCEPTANCE.

CLAIM | "Acceptances are carried forward verbatim -- refreshing is never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason" | refresh | KEPT | refresh loads old snapshot, parses acceptances, and passes them to write_snapshot.
CLAIM | "Fail CLOSED, matching ``daedalus map --check``" | main | KEPT | When report.first_run is True, main returns 1.

CLAIM | "This used to write the baseline and exit 0, which made ``rm docs/architecture-state.json`` a green run through a door reach.py itself classifies as an entry point" | main | KEPT | The docstring describes the old behavior; the current code returns 1 for first_run, matching the new behavior described.

CLAIM | "Explicit on purpose: a missing snapshot fails, so deleting it is never a green run" | main | KEPT | The --init flag uses write_missing=True, and if the snapshot already exists, it returns 1; otherwise it writes and exits 0. The docstring for --init says the same.

CLAIM | "A count matching its own list proves only internal arithmetic. These check the lists against reality and against each other, so an entry cannot be pre-seeded to suppress a finding that has not landed yet" | check | KEPT | The code checks phantom_islands, phantom for unknown and shims, phantom_test_only, and phantom_dark against the current state, not just counts.

CLAIM | "An accepted island is deliberately absent from the baseline (:func:`write_snapshot`), so the baseline alone would read it as 'reached' and call it BECAME ISLAND the moment the module also appears in ``modules``" | check | KEPT | The comment explains this; the code uses accepted_keys to include accepted items in known_unreached.

CLAIM | "The acceptance is itself a record that it is an island, so it counts toward what the snapshot knows -- without suppressing anything" | check | KEPT | accepted_keys are part of known_unreached, so they are not treated as newly unreached.

CLAIM | "Intersecting with ``modules`` is the teeth behind the subset rule above: an island entry the snapshot's own module list does not back is a hand-edit, and a hand-edit must not be able to suppress the finding it was written to hide" | check | KEPT | baselined_islands = old_islands & old_modules, so only modules that appear in both are considered baselined.

CLAIM | "A module the snapshot recorded as unknown or as an unreached shim was never reached, so it must not be described that way when it degrades into an island" | check | KEPT | known_unreached includes old_islands, old_unknown, old_shims intersected with old_modules, so they are not treated as was_reached.

CLAIM | "A missing snapshot FAILS unless ``write_missing`` is set" | check | KEPT | The code returns DriftReport(ok=False, first_run=True) with empty items when snapshot is None and write_missing is False, which counts as a failure.

CLAIM | "The previous default -- write it and report OK -- meant ``rm docs/architecture-state.json`` was a green run" | check docstring | KEPT | The docstring describes a historical behavior that is no longer present; the code does not implement that default, so the claim is accurate about the past.

CLAIM | "Explicit on purpose: a missing snapshot fails, so deleting it is never a green run" | main --init help | KEPT | The --init flag explicitly requires --init to write the first baseline; without it, missing snapshot causes failure (return 1).

CLAIM | "Acceptances are carried forward verbatim -- refreshing is never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason." | refresh docstring | BROKEN | Line: `acceptances = parse_acceptances(old.get("acceptances"))` does not pass `today` argument, so acceptances are parsed without a date context, potentially altering their validity and thus not carrying them forward verbatim.
CLAIM | "Fail CLOSED, matching `daedalus map --check`. This used to write the baseline and exit 0" | main comment | KEPT | The code returns 1 when report.first_run is True, failing closed as stated.

CLAIM | "An ABSENT key reads as 'nothing was excluded', not as 'do not check'. Deleting the field must not be a quieter way to narrow the run than setting the variable was." | comment in check | KEPT | The code sets old_ignore to a default dict with empty strings when the key is missing or not a dict, treating absence as no exclusion.

D1 | acceptances (in refresh) | `today` parameter not passed to parse_acceptances | WRONG CONCLUSION: a caller believes acceptances are carried forward verbatim, but they may be re-parsed without date context, potentially changing their validity.
